title: Documents to Gather Before Your Consult
description: A list of the papers and details to pull together before your first estate planning meeting, so the meeting can focus on decisions.
intro: Bringing the right papers to your first meeting saves time and helps your attorney see the full picture. You do not need every item on this list. Gather what you can and note what you could not find.

sections.heading: Existing plan documents
items: Current will and any codicils
Any trust agreements and amendments
Financial power of attorney
Health care power of attorney and living will
Prenuptial or postnuptial agreement
Divorce decree or property settlement, if any

sections.heading: Real estate
items: Deed for your home
Deeds for rental, vacation, or out-of-state property
Recent mortgage statement for each property
Property tax bill or assessed value for each property

sections.heading: Financial accounts
items: Most recent statement for each bank account
Most recent statement for each brokerage or investment account
Retirement account statements, such as 401(k), 403(b), and IRA
Pension or annuity statements
Notes on any cryptocurrency or online-only accounts

sections.heading: Insurance and beneficiary forms
items: Life insurance policy declarations pages
Beneficiary designation forms for each policy and retirement account
Long-term care insurance policy
Disability insurance policy

sections.heading: Business and debts
items: Business operating agreement, bylaws, or partnership agreement
Buy-sell agreement, if any
List of loans, credit cards, and other debts with rough balances
Any money you have lent to family members

sections.heading: People and decisions
items: Full names and contact details for your spouse, children, and grandchildren
Names of people you are considering as executor, trustee, and agents
Names of people you are considering as guardian for minor children
Notes on any family member with special needs, health issues, or money troubles
Charities you may want to include
